sections.name: stageContractSchema
sections.title: Stage record format
sections.what: Defines the required fields for a stage record and the only allowed states: running, succeeded, failed, cancelled and interrupted. The input fingerprint must be exactly 64 characters.
sections.why: Likely reason: consistent records let later code trust what it reads.
sections.watch_out: Adding a state here means every reader that checks states must also handle the new one.

sections.name: stageContract
sections.title: Opening a stage record
sections.what: Creates the opening record for a stage: fingerprints its input, sets the attempt number and start time, and marks it running with no finish time.
sections.why: Likely reason: the fingerprint lets a later run tell whether the inputs changed.
sections.watch_out: The fingerprint depends on the exact JSON text of the input, so reordering keys counts as a change.

sections.name: stageSummary
sections.title: Closing a stage record
sections.what: Takes a stage's result data and attaches a closing record marked succeeded with a finish time, under a key starting with an underscore.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the result and its record together in one saved object.
sections.watch_out: This always marks the stage succeeded, so a failed stage must not be passed through it.

summary: Defines the record kept for each processing stage of a research run, including a fingerprint of its input and the final state when it succeeds.
purpose: Lets the app record each stage's start, finish, state and input fingerprint so a run can be checked or resumed.
why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: a fixed record format makes stage records consistent for later code.
how: First, the schema defines required fields and the allowed states: running, succeeded, failed, cancelled and interrupted. Second, creating a stage record fingerprints its input data with SHA-256 and marks it running with no finish time. Third, closing a stage attaches a record marked succeeded with a finish time to the result data.
inputs: Run identifier, stage name, input data, attempt number, start time, a result payload, the opening record and a finish time.
outputs: A checked stage record, and a result payload with that record attached under a key starting with an underscore.
risks: Invalid data throws a schema error, and no error handling is visible. Fingerprints depend on the order of keys in the input, so reordering keys counts as a change. This file only marks stages succeeded, so failed and other states are set elsewhere.
debug: If saving a stage fails, read the schema error, which names the field. Check that times are valid timestamps and the fingerprint is 64 characters. If a stage reruns unexpectedly, compare its input fingerprints.
